Working with skills

Source: vignettes/skills.qmd

What is a skill?

A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file inside it. The file starts with a short header giving the skill a name and a one-sentence description of when it applies, followed by instructions written in plain Markdown. Some skills also carry supporting files alongside SKILL.md: reference documents, templates, or worked examples the instructions point to.

AI coding assistants such as Claude Code and Codex look for skills in a known folder in your project. When you ask for something that matches a skill’s description, the assistant reads the instructions and follows them. Without a skill, the assistant has to guess how you like things done. With one, it knows.

Posit’s Quarto authoring skill is a good example. Its description says to use it whenever you are working with .qmd files or Quarto projects, and its instructions and reference files cover callouts, cross-references, citations, and the other details an assistant tends to get wrong.

Skills live on GitHub, but installing one usually means npm or copying folders by hand. {ally} does it from R.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rfortherestofus/ally")

Install your first skill

Open the project you want the skill in, copy the link to the skill’s SKILL.md from your browser, and paste it into install_skill():

library(ally)

install_skill(
  "https://github.com/posit-dev/skills/blob/main/quarto/quarto-authoring/SKILL.md"
)
#> ✔ Installed "quarto-authoring" to '~/projects/report/.agents/skills/quarto-authoring'
#> ℹ Codex and other agents read '.agents/skills/' directly.
#> ✔ Copied to "Claude Code" ('~/projects/report/.claude/skills')

That is the whole workflow. Open the project in Claude Code or Codex, ask for help with a Quarto document, and the assistant picks the skill up on its own.

Where the files go

install_skill() puts the skill in two places inside the project:

Path What it is
.agents/skills/<skill>/ The canonical copy. Codex and a growing number of agents read it directly.
.claude/skills/<skill>/ A second copy for Claude Code, which only looks in its own folder.

Both folders are plain directories, so they can be committed to git and shared with collaborators.

A walkthrough you can run

Everything below runs against a throwaway project and a skill written on the fly, so it works offline and touches nothing else on your computer.

library(ally)

# A minimal skill: a folder with a SKILL.md inside it
skill <- fs::dir_create(fs::path(tempdir(), "r-style-guide"))
writeLines(
  c(
    "---",
    "name: r-style-guide",
    "description: House style for R code in this project.",
    "---",
    "",
    "Follow the tidyverse style guide. Use the base pipe `|>`."
  ),
  fs::path(skill, "SKILL.md")
)

# An empty project to install it into
project <- fs::dir_create(fs::path(tempdir(), "my-project"))

Install from the local path. The project is set as the working directory just for this call:

withr::with_dir(project, install_skill(skill))
#> ✔ Installed "r-style-guide" to '/tmp/RtmpGOBgVu/my-project/.agents/skills/r-style-guide'
#> ℹ Codex and other agents read '.agents/skills/' directly.
#> ✔ Copied to "Claude Code" ('/tmp/RtmpGOBgVu/my-project/.claude/skills')

Both copies are now in place:

fs::dir_tree(project, all = TRUE)
#> /tmp/RtmpGOBgVu/my-project
#> ├── .agents
#> │   └── skills
#> │       └── r-style-guide
#> │           ├── .ally-source.json
#> │           └── SKILL.md
#> └── .claude
#>     └── skills
#>         └── r-style-guide
#>             ├── .ally-source.json
#>             └── SKILL.md

installed_skills() lists what is installed in a project:

withr::with_dir(project, installed_skills())
#> [1] "r-style-guide"

And remove_skill() deletes both copies:

withr::with_dir(project, remove_skill("r-style-guide"))
#> ✔ Removed copy at '/tmp/RtmpGOBgVu/my-project/.claude/skills/r-style-guide'
#> ✔ Removed canonical copy at '/tmp/RtmpGOBgVu/my-project/.agents/skills/r-style-guide'

This project or every project

By default a skill is installed into the current working directory, so it travels with the project. Pass scope = "user" to install it into your home folder instead, where every project on the computer can use it:

install_skill("posit-dev/skills/quarto/quarto-authoring", scope = "user")
#> ✔ Installed "quarto-authoring" to '~/.agents/skills/quarto-authoring'
#> ℹ Every project on this computer can use skills in '~/.agents/skills/'.
#> ✔ Copied to "Claude Code" ('~/.claude/skills')

Every function in {ally} takes the same scope argument.

Ways to name a skill

install_skill() accepts a few forms of source:

# A full GitHub URL, pasted straight from the browser
install_skill(
  "https://github.com/posit-dev/skills/tree/main/quarto/quarto-authoring"
)

# The link to the SKILL.md itself also works
install_skill(
  "https://github.com/posit-dev/skills/blob/main/quarto/quarto-authoring/SKILL.md"
)

# A repository whose SKILL.md sits at the top level is named after the repository
install_skill("https://github.com/statzhero/tidy-r-skill")

# GitHub shorthand: owner/repo/path/to/skill, with an optional @ref
install_skill("posit-dev/skills/quarto/quarto-authoring")
install_skill("owner/repo/skills/my-skill@dev")

# A local path, handy while writing a skill of your own
install_skill("~/my-skills/r-style-guide")

GitHub skills are fetched from the repository’s zip archive: a single download that needs no token and never counts against the GitHub API rate limit, so a room full of people on one network can install at once. Public repositories only.

Keeping skills current

Skills change. Authors fix mistakes, add reference material, and adapt their instructions as the tools they describe evolve. The Quarto authoring skill, for instance, records a version number in its SKILL.md header and has been revised several times. An installed skill is a snapshot of the moment you installed it; it does not update itself.

{ally} records where each skill came from in a small .ally-source.json file next to the SKILL.md, so getting the newest version is one call:

update_skill("quarto-authoring")
#> ℹ Updating "quarto-authoring" from "posit-dev/skills/quarto/quarto-authoring@main"
#> ✔ Installed "quarto-authoring" to '~/projects/report/.agents/skills/quarto-authoring'
#> ℹ Codex and other agents read '.agents/skills/' directly.
#> ✔ Copied to "Claude Code" ('~/projects/report/.claude/skills')

update_skill() fetches the skill again from its original source, replaces the canonical copy, and refreshes the Claude Code copy. To bring every skill in a project up to date at once:

for (skill in installed_skills()) {
  update_skill(skill)
}

Skills installed with scope = "user" are updated the same way, with scope = "user" added to each call.

If you edit a skill by hand in .agents/skills/, or delete the Claude Code copy by accident, link_skills() refreshes the copies for every installed skill without fetching anything:

link_skills()

Prefer a single set of files? Pass link = TRUE to install_skill(), update_skill(), or link_skills() and {ally} puts a relative symlink at .claude/skills/<skill> pointing back to the canonical copy instead of a second copy. Where symlinks are not supported (typically Windows without developer mode) it falls back to copying and tells you so.

Where to find skills

  • Ally from R for the Rest of Us offers a curated collection of skills for R users working with AI. Each one comes with the link to paste into install_skill().
  • posit-dev/skills is Posit’s collection, covering R packages, Shiny, Quarto, and more.
  • Write your own. A folder with a SKILL.md is all it takes, and install_skill() accepts a local path while you iterate.
